25	# Number of CPUs reserved per Verilate action in Bazel's local scheduler.
26	# Sourced from `nproc` at workspace-fetch time so we don't oversubscribe
27	# small hosts (a hardcoded 8 was blocking 6-core boxes from scheduling
28	# more than one action at a time).

31	def _verilator_resource_estimator(os, input_size):
32	    # Cap the scheduler reservation at 4 so multiple actions can still run
33	    # in parallel on larger hosts; the `make -j` inside the action is free
34	    # to use more threads if the scheduler hands them over.
35	    return {"cpu": min(_verilator_make_parallelism, 4), "memory": 4096}

37	def _verilator_cocotb_model_impl(ctx):
38	    hdl_toplevel = ctx.attr.hdl_toplevel
39	    outdir_name = hdl_toplevel + "_build"

41	    cc_toolchain = find_cc_toolchain(ctx)
42	    compiler_executable = cc_toolchain.compiler_executable
43	    ar_executable = cc_toolchain.ar_executable
44	    ld_executable = cc_toolchain.ld_executable
45	
46	    # Collect DPI/C++ dependencies
47	    dpi_srcs_dict = {}
48	    dpi_includes = []
49	    dpi_files_dict = {}
50	    verilog_srcs = []
51	
52	    def add_dpi_src(f):
53	        if type(f) == "File" and f.extension in ["cc", "cpp", "cxx", "c", "a", "o"]:
54	            dpi_srcs_dict[f.path] = "$PWD/" + f.path
55	            dpi_files_dict[f.path] = f
56	
57	    def add_dpi_file(f):
58	        if type(f) == "File":
59	            dpi_files_dict[f.path] = f
60	
61	    # We need to collect CC sources transitively
62	    for dep in ctx.attr.deps:
63	        if CcInfo in dep:
64	            cc_info = dep[CcInfo]
65	
66	            # Transitive includes
67	            for inc in cc_info.compilation_context.includes.to_list():
68	                dpi_includes.append("-I" + inc)
69	            for inc in cc_info.compilation_context.quote_includes.to_list():
70	                dpi_includes.append("-I" + inc)
71	            for inc in cc_info.compilation_context.system_includes.to_list():
72	                dpi_includes.append("-I" + inc)
73	
74	            # Transitive headers
75	            for f in cc_info.compilation_context.headers.to_list():
76	                add_dpi_file(f)
77	
78	            # Transitive sources
79	            # Bazel rules often put sources in DefaultInfo
80	            for f in dep[DefaultInfo].files.to_list():
81	                add_dpi_src(f)
82	                if f.extension in ["h", "hh", "hpp"]:
83	                    add_dpi_file(f)
84	
85	            # Check transitive linker inputs for sources that might be hidden
86	            # This is necessary for targets that don't have sources in DefaultInfo
87	            for li in cc_info.linking_context.linker_inputs.to_list():
88	                for lib in li.libraries:
89	                    if lib.static_library:
90	                        add_dpi_file(lib.static_library)
91	                    if lib.pic_static_library:
92	                        add_dpi_file(lib.pic_static_library)
93	                    if lib.objects:
94	                        for obj in lib.objects:
95	                            add_dpi_file(obj)
96	
97	        if VerilogInfo in dep:
98	            verilog_srcs.append(dep[VerilogInfo].dag)
99	
100	    # Collect all input files for the action and their paths
101	    all_inputs_dict = {}
102	    verilog_paths = []
103	
104	    def add_input(f):
105	        if type(f) == "File":
106	            all_inputs_dict[f.path] = f
107	            return True
108	        return False
109	
110	    for f in dpi_files_dict.values():
111	        add_input(f)
112	
113	    # Process verilog sources collected from deps and direct attributes
114	    for f in verilog_srcs:
115	        if type(f) == "File":
116	            if add_input(f):
117	                verilog_paths.append(f.path)
118	        elif hasattr(f, "to_list"):  # It's a depset from VerilogInfo.dag
119	            for node in f.to_list():
120	                for s in node.srcs:
121	                    if add_input(s):
122	                        verilog_paths.append(s.path)
123	
124	    if ctx.attr.verilog_source:
125	        f = ctx.file.verilog_source
126	        add_input(f)
127	        verilog_paths.append(f.path)
128	
129	    for f in ctx.files.verilog_sources:

132	
133	    vlt_file = ctx.actions.declare_file(hdl_toplevel + ".vlt")
134	    ctx.actions.expand_template(
135	        output = vlt_file,
136	        template = ctx.file.vlt_tpl,

138	    )
139	    add_input(vlt_file)
140	
141	    output_file = ctx.actions.declare_file(outdir_name + "/" + hdl_toplevel)
142	    make_log = ctx.actions.declare_file(outdir_name + "/make.log")
143	    outdir = output_file.dirname
144	
145	    verilator_root = "$PWD/{}.runfiles/coralnpu_hw/external/verilator".format(ctx.executable._verilator_bin.path)
146	    cocotb_lib_path = "$PWD/{}".format(ctx.files._cocotb_verilator_lib[0].dirname)
147	
148	    # Prepend $PWD to paths for verilator to find them in the sandbox
149	    verilog_sources_str = " ".join(["$PWD/" + p if not p.startswith("/") else p for p in verilog_paths])
150	
151	    verilator_cmd = " ".join("""
152	        VERILATOR_ROOT={verilator_root} {verilator} \
153	            -cc \
154	            --exe \
155	            -Mdir {outdir} \
156	            --top-module {hdl_toplevel} \
157	            --vpi \
158	            --prefix Vtop \
159	            -o {hdl_toplevel} \
160	            -LDFLAGS "-Wl,-rpath {cocotb_lib_path} -L{cocotb_lib_path} -lcocotbvpi_verilator" \
161	            {trace} \
162	            {cflags} \
163	            -I. -Ihdl/verilog {dpi_includes} \
164	            $PWD/{verilator_cpp} \
165	            $PWD/{vlt_file} \
166	            {dpi_srcs} \
167	            {verilog_sources}
168	    """.strip().split("\n")).format(
169	        verilator = ctx.executable._verilator_bin.path,
170	        verilator_root = verilator_root,
171	        outdir = outdir,
172	        hdl_toplevel = hdl_toplevel,
173	        cocotb_lib_path = cocotb_lib_path,
174	        cflags = " ".join(ctx.attr.cflags),
175	        dpi_includes = " ".join({inc: None for inc in dpi_includes}.keys()),  # Unique includes
176	        verilator_cpp = ctx.files._cocotb_verilator_cpp[0].path,
177	        vlt_file = vlt_file.path,
178	        dpi_srcs = " ".join(dpi_srcs_dict.values()),
179	        verilog_sources = verilog_sources_str,
180	        trace = "--trace" if ctx.attr.trace else "",
181	    )

183	    make_cmd = "PATH=`dirname {ld}`:$PATH make -j {parallelism} -C {outdir} -f Vtop.mk {trace} CXX={cxx} AR={ar} LINK={cxx} > {make_log} 2>&1".format(
184	        outdir = outdir,
185	        cocotb_lib_path = cocotb_lib_path,
186	        make_log = make_log.path,
187	        trace = "VM_TRACE=1" if ctx.attr.trace else "",
188	        ar = ar_executable,
189	        ld = ld_executable,
190	        cxx = compiler_executable,
191	        parallelism = _verilator_make_parallelism,
192	    )

194	    script = " && ".join([verilator_cmd.strip(), make_cmd])

196	    ctx.actions.run_shell(
197	        outputs = [output_file, make_log],
198	        tools = ctx.files._verilator_bin,

208	        mnemonic = "Verilate",
209	        resource_set = _verilator_resource_estimator,
210	    )

213	        DefaultInfo(
214	            files = depset([output_file, make_log]),
215	            runfiles = ctx.runfiles(files = [output_file, make_log]),
216	            executable = output_file,
217	        ),
218	        OutputGroupInfo(
219	            all_files = depset([output_file, make_log]),

59	    """Implements compilation for coralnpu executables.
60	
61	    This rule compiles and links provided input into an executable
62	    suitable for use on the CoralNPU core. Generates an ELF.
63	
64	    Args:
65	      ctx: context for the rules.
66	        srcs: Input source files.

70	        defines: Preprocessor definitions.

75	        containing the output ELF and BIN.

78	    if type(cc_toolchain) != 'CcToolchainInfo':
79	        cc_toolchain = cc_toolchain.cc
80	    feature_configuration = cc_common.configure_features(
81	        ctx = ctx,
82	        cc_toolchain = cc_toolchain,
83	        requested_features = ctx.features,
84	        unsupported_features = ctx.disabled_features,
85	    )
86	    compilation_contexts = []
87	    linking_contexts = []
88	    for dep in ctx.attr.deps:
89	        if CcInfo in dep:
90	            compilation_contexts.append(dep[CcInfo].compilation_context)
91	            linking_contexts.append(dep[CcInfo].linking_context)
92	
93	    sources = []
94	    headers = []
95	    for src in ctx.files.srcs:
96	        if src.extension in ["h", "hh", "hpp"]:
97	            headers.append(src)
98	        else:
99	            sources.append(src)
100	
101	    (_compilation_context, compilation_outputs) = cc_common.compile(
102	        actions = ctx.actions,
103	        cc_toolchain = cc_toolchain,
104	        feature_configuration = feature_configuration,
105	        name = ctx.label.name,
106	        srcs = sources,
107	        compilation_contexts = compilation_contexts,
108	        private_hdrs = headers + ctx.files.hdrs,
109	        user_compile_flags = ctx.attr.copts,
110	        defines = ctx.attr.defines,
111	    )
112	    linking_outputs = cc_common.link(
113	        name = "{}.elf".format(ctx.label.name),
114	        actions = ctx.actions,
115	        feature_configuration = feature_configuration,
116	        cc_toolchain = cc_toolchain,
117	        compilation_outputs = compilation_outputs,
118	        linking_contexts = linking_contexts,

140	    )

22	class FIFOStateTestWrapper(t: UInt, n: Int, capacity: Int) extends Module {
23	  val io = IO(new Bundle {
24	    val enqValid = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n+1).W))
25	    val enqData = Input(Vec(n, t))
26	    val deqReady = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n+1).W))
27	    val flush = Input(Bool())
28	
29	    val nEnqueued = Output(UInt(log2Ceil(capacity+1).W))
30	    val dataOut = Output(Vec(n, t))
31	  })
32	
33	  val state = RegInit(FIFOState.init(capacity, t))
34	
35	  // Chain: Dequeue then Enqueue to handle simultaneous operations with maximum throughput
36	  val deqState = state.dequeue(io.deqReady)
37	  val enqState = deqState.enqueue(io.enqData, io.enqValid)
38	
39	  state := Mux(io.flush, state.flush(), enqState)
40	  // Assert that the state is consistent after every cycle
41	  assert(state.invariant())
42	
43	  io.nEnqueued := state.count
44	  io.dataOut := state.peek(n)
45	}

110	        val shiftedData: BigInt = c.data << (c.addr * 8)
111	        val alignedAddr = c.addr - (c.addr % c.size)
112	
113	        dut.io.axi.read.addr.ready.poke(false.B)
114	        dut.io.axi.read.data.valid.poke(false.B)
115	        dut.io.axi.write.data.ready.poke(false.B)
116	        dut.io.axi.write.addr.ready.poke(false.B)
117	        dut.io.axi.write.resp.valid.poke(false.B)
118	        dut.clock.step()

121	        dut.io.dbus.valid.poke(true.B)
122	        dut.io.dbus.addr.poke(c.addr.U)
123	        dut.io.dbus.write.poke(true.B)
124	        dut.io.dbus.wdata.poke(shiftedData.U(p.axi2DataBits.W))
125	        dut.io.dbus.wmask.poke(c.mask.U)
126	        dut.io.dbus.size.poke(c.size.U)

128	        val (waddr, wsize, wlen) = {
129	          dut.io.axi.write.addr.ready.poke(true.B)
130	          while (dut.io.axi.write.addr.valid.peek().litValue != 1 || dut.io.axi.write.addr.ready.peek().litValue != 1) {
131	            dut.clock.step()
132	          }
133	          val rv = (
134	            dut.io.axi.write.addr.bits.addr.peek().litValue,
135	            dut.io.axi.write.addr.bits.size.peek().litValue,
136	            dut.io.axi.write.addr.bits.len.peek().litValue,
137	          )
138	          dut.clock.step()
139	          dut.io.axi.write.addr.ready.poke(false.B)
140	          rv
141	        }

143	        assertResult(waddr) { alignedAddr }
144	        assertResult(wsize) { log2Ceil(c.size) }
145	        assertResult(wlen) { 0 }
146	
147	        val (wdata, wstrb) = {
148	          dut.io.axi.write.data.ready.poke(true.B)
149	          while (dut.io.axi.write.data.valid.peek().litValue != 1 || dut.io.axi.write.data.ready.peek().litValue != 1) {
150	            dut.clock.step()

154	            dut.io.axi.write.data.bits.data.peek().litValue,

156	          )
157	          dut.clock.step()
158	          dut.io.axi.write.data.ready.poke(false.B)
159	          rv

168	          dut.io.axi.write.resp.bits.resp.poke(0.U)

179	        dut.io.dbus.valid.poke(true.B)

181	        dut.io.dbus.write.poke(false.B)
182	        dut.io.dbus.size.poke(c.size.U)

187	          dut.io.axi.read.addr.ready.poke(true.B)
188	          while (dut.io.axi.read.addr.valid.peek().litValue != 1 || dut.io.axi.read.addr.ready.peek().litValue != 1) {
189	            dut.clock.step()

193	            dut.io.axi.read.addr.bits.addr.peek().litValue,
194	            dut.io.axi.read.addr.bits.size.peek().litValue,
195	          )
196	          dut.clock.step()
197	          dut.io.axi.read.addr.ready.poke(false.B)
198	          rv

202	        assertResult(size) { log2Ceil(c.size) }
203	        assertResult(addr) { c.addr }

207	          for (i <- 0 to (len).toInt) {
208	            dut.io.axi.read.data.valid.poke(true)

17	// A starting functions for simple coralnpu programs.
18	
19	.extern coralnpu_exception_handler
20	.extern __fini_array_start__
21	.extern __fini_array_end__
22	
23	/**
24	 * Entry point.
25	 */
26	        .section ._init
27	        .balign 4
28	        .global _start
29	        .weak _start
30	        .type _start, @function
31	_start:
32	        csrw minstret, 0
33	        csrw minstreth, 0
34	        csrr a0, minstret
35	        csrr a1, minstreth
36	        ###############################################
37	        # Put all scalar registers into a known state #
38	        ###############################################
39	.option norelax
40	        la   sp, __stack_end__
41	        la   gp, _global_pointer
42	.option relax
43	
44	        mv   tp, zero
45	        mv   t1, zero
46	        mv   t2, zero
47	        mv   s0, zero
48	        mv   s1, zero
49	        mv   a1, zero
50	        mv   a2, zero
51	        mv   a3, zero
52	        mv   a4, zero
53	        mv   a5, zero
54	        mv   a6, zero
55	        mv   a7, zero
56	        mv   s2, zero
57	        mv   s3, zero
58	        mv   s4, zero
59	        mv   s5, zero
60	        mv   s6, zero
61	        mv   s7, zero
62	        mv   s8, zero
63	        mv   s9, zero
64	        mv   s10, zero
65	        mv   s11, zero
66	        mv   t3, zero
67	        mv   t4, zero
68	        mv   t5, zero
69	        mv   t6, zero
70	
71	        # Zero out the bss section
72	        la   a0, __bss_start__
73	        la   a1, __bss_end__
74	        call crt_section_clear
75	
76	        # Run constructors
77	        la   s0, __init_array_start__
78	        la   s1, __init_array_end__
79	        bgeu s0, s1, init_array_loop_end
80	init_array_loop:
81	        lw   t0, 0(s0)
82	        jalr t0
83	        addi s0, s0, 0x4
84	        bltu s0, s1, init_array_loop
85	init_array_loop_end:
86	
87	        # Set up a default trap vector, which will
88	        # simply call ebreak.
89	        # Users who require real trap handling should
90	        # install their own trap vector.
91	        la t0, coralnpu_exception_handler
92	        csrw mtvec, t0
93	
94	        # Set FS (0x6000) and VS (0x600) to Dirty
95	        li      t0, 0x6600
96	        csrrs   zero, mstatus, t0
97	
98	        # Set up sentinel value in _ret
99	        # If we see this after an ebreak,
100	        # the break source is unlikely to
101	        # be a clean return from main.
102	        la   t0, _ret
103	        li   a0, 0x0badd00d
104	        sw   a0, 0(t0)
105	
106	        #############
107	        # Call main #
108	        #############
109	        li   a0, 0  # argv
110	        li   a1, 0  # argc
111	        la   ra, main
112	        jalr ra, ra
113	        # Save return value
114	        mv   s2, a0
115	
116	        # Call C++ finalizers
117	        call __cxa_finalize
118	
119	        # Initialize finalization arrays (destructors)
120	        # These are called in reverse order.
121	        la   s0, __fini_array_start__
122	        la   s1, __fini_array_end__
123	        beq  s0, s1, fini_array_loop_end
124	fini_array_loop:
125	        addi s1, s1, -0x4
126	        lw   t0, 0(s1)
127	        jalr t0
128	        bne  s0, s1, fini_array_loop
129	fini_array_loop_end:
130	
131	        # Restore the application's return value
132	        mv   a0, s2
133	        la   t0, _ret
134	        sw   a0, 0(t0)
135	        beqz a0, success
136	failure:
137	        ebreak
138	        j    loop
139	success:
140	        # Commit instruction retirement counters to architectural state.
141	        # This is for co-simulation verification purposes.
142	        csrr a0, minstret
143	        csrr a1, minstreth
144	        .word 0x08000073 # mpause
145	loop:
146	        j    loop

17	/**
18	 * CRT library
19	 *
20	 * Utility functions written in assembly that can be used before the C
21	 * runtime has been initialized. These functions should not be used once
22	 * the C runtime has been initialized.
23	 *
24	 * The name of this library is historical. In many toolchains, a file called
25	 * "crt0.o" is linked into each executable, which does something similar to
26	 * what these functions
27	 */
28	
29	  // NOTE: The "ax" flag below is necessary to ensure that this section
30	  // is allocated space in ROM by the linker.
31	  .section .crt, "ax", @progbits
32	
33	  /**
34	   * Write zeros into the section bounded by the start and end pointers.
35	   * The section must be word (4 byte) aligned. It is valid for the section
36	   * to have a length of 0 (i.e. the start and end pointers may be equal).
37	   *
38	   * This function follows the standard ILP32 calling convention for arguments
39	   * but does not require a valid stack pointer, thread pointer or global
40	   * pointer.
41	   *
42	   * Clobbers a0 and t0.
43	   *
44	   * @param a0 pointer to start of section to clear (inclusive).
45	   * @param a1 pointer to end of section to clear (exclusive).
46	   */
47	  .balign 4
48	  .global crt_section_clear
49	  .type crt_section_clear, @function
50	crt_section_clear:
51	
52	  // Check that start is before end.
53	  bgeu a0, a1, .L_clear_nothing
54	
55	  // Check that start and end are word aligned.
56	  or   t0, a0, a1
57	  andi t0, t0, 0x3
58	  bnez t0, .L_clear_error
59	
60	.L_clear_loop:
61	  // Write zero into section memory word-by-word.
62	  // TODO: unroll
63	  sw   zero, 0(a0)
64	  addi a0, a0, 4
65	  bltu a0, a1, .L_clear_loop
66	  ret
67	
68	.L_clear_nothing:
69	  // If section length is 0 just return. Otherwise end is before start
70	  // which is invalid so trigger an error.
71	  bne a0, a1, .L_clear_error
72	  ret
73	
74	.L_clear_error:
75	  ebreak
76	
77	  // Set function size to allow disassembly.
78	  .size crt_section_clear, .-crt_section_clear
79	
80	// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
81	
82	  /**
83	   * Copy data from the given source into the section bounded by the start and
84	   * end pointers. Both the section and the source must be word (4 byte) aligned.
85	   * It is valid for the section to have a length of 0 (i.e. the start and end
86	   * pointers may be equal). The source is assumed to have the same length as the
87	   * target section.
88	   *
89	   * The destination section and the source must not overlap.
90	   *
91	   * This function follows the standard ILP32 calling convention for arguments
92	   * but does not require a valid stack pointer, thread pointer or global
93	   * pointer.
94	   *
95	   * Clobbers a0, a2, t0 and t1.
96	   *
97	   * @param a0 pointer to start of destination section (inclusive).
98	   * @param a1 pointer to end of destination section (exclusive).
99	   * @param a2 pointer to source data (inclusive).
100	   */
101	  .balign 4
102	  .global crt_section_copy
103	  .type crt_section_copy, @function
104	crt_section_copy:
105	
106	  // Check that start is before end.
107	  bgeu a0, a1, .L_copy_nothing
108	
109	  // Check that start, end and src are word aligned.
110	  or   t0, a0, a1
111	  or   t0, t0, a2
112	  andi t0, t0, 0x3
113	  bnez t0, .L_copy_error
114	
115	  // Check that source does not destructively overlap destination
116	  // (assuming a forwards copy).
117	  //
118	  // src  start          end
119	  //  |     |             |
120	  //  +-------------+     |
121	  //  |   source    |     |
122	  //  +-------------+     |
123	  //        +-------------+
124	  //        | destination |
125	  //        +-------------+
126	  //        |             |
127	  //      start          end
128	  //
129	  // TODO: disallow all overlap since it indicates API misuse?
130	  sub  t0, a0, a2           // (start - src) mod 2**32
131	  sub  t1, a1, a0           // end - start
132	  bltu t0, t1, .L_copy_error
133	
134	.L_copy_loop:
135	  // Copy data from src into section word-by-word.
136	  // TODO: unroll
137	  lw   t0, 0(a2)
138	  addi a2, a2, 4
139	  sw   t0, 0(a0)
140	  addi a0, a0, 4
141	  bltu a0, a1, .L_copy_loop
142	  ret
143	
144	.L_copy_nothing:
145	  // If section length is 0 just return. Otherwise end is before start
146	  // which is invalid so trigger an error.
147	  bne a0, a1, .L_copy_error
148	  ret
149	
150	.L_copy_error:

### /app/toolchain/crt/coralnpu_start.S — Behavior

`_start` (in `._init`, weak): clears `minstret`/`minstreth`, reads them into a0/a1, sets `sp=__stack_end__`, `gp=_global_pointer`, zeros all GPRs (tp/t1/t2/s0/s1/a1..a7/s2..s11/t3..t6), zeros `.bss` via `crt_section_clear`, runs `__init_array_*`, sets `mtvec` to `coralnpu_exception_handler`, sets FS+VS bits in mstatus (`0x6600`), seeds `_ret` with `0x0badd00d`, calls `main(argv=0, argc=0)`, calls `__cxa_finalize`, runs reverse `__fini_array_*`, stores return value in `_ret`.
